title: Repeating with for
content:
What problem does this solve?
A list can grow. Visiting item1, item2, item3 by hand does not scale. A for loop runs the same block once for each value in a list.

Basic syntax
  for item in inventory:
      print(item)

What actually happens
Python takes the first value in inventory, binds it to item, and runs the indented block. Then it repeats with the next value, until the list is finished.

When this is useful
Use a for loop whenever you want to do the same thing to every item — print them, check them, or format a line for each one.
concepts: for item in a_list repeats a block once per value
The loop variable holds the current item, not an index
The indented block is the work that repeats

examples.title: Print every item
examples.explanation: The block runs twice: first with sword, then with shield.

common_mistakes: Forgetting the colon after the for line
Forgetting to indent the repeated line
Printing the whole list once instead of looping over items

exercises.title: Predict the loop
exercises.prompt: What does this print? Type each line of output.
hints: The loop body runs once per item, in order.
Each print ends a line, so you get one name per line.

exercises.title: List the party
exercises.prompt: party is already created. Print each member on its own line, in order, using a for loop.
hints: for some_name in party: repeats a block for each value.
Print the loop variable, not the whole list.
One print inside the loop is enough.

tests.message: Use a for loop to visit each party member.

exercises.title: Label each item
exercises.prompt:
inventory is already created. For each item, print a line like:
- sword

Use a for loop and an f-string. The three lines should be:
- sword
- shield
- potion
exercises.starter_code:
inventory = ["sword", "shield", "potion"]
# Print a labeled line for each item
hints: Loop over inventory so item is each string in turn.
An f-string can start with - and insert the current item.
Print once inside the loop, not three separate print calls.

tests.message: Use a for loop so the work repeats for each item.
Build each line with an f-string.
